hero.headline: Trump delays intelligence chief nomination, ties confirmation to voting legislation
hero.body:
President Trump announced Wednesday that he is pausing the confirmation process for Jay Clayton, his nominee for Director of National Intelligence, until Congress passes legislation on warrantless surveillance powers and voter identification requirements. The Senate had been scheduled to begin confirmation hearings for Clayton, a federal prosecutor, on Wednesday.

Trump said Clayton's hearing would be delayed until Congress approves both the extension of warrantless spy powers and a voter identification bill. The president indicated that acting Director of National Intelligence Bill Pulte will remain in the position during the delay. Trump had originally nominated Clayton to address concerns from lawmakers that Pulte lacked sufficient experience for the intelligence role.

The move links a key national security appointment to unrelated legislative priorities. The warrantless surveillance powers in question allow intelligence agencies to collect communications of foreign targets without obtaining individual warrants, a program that requires periodic congressional reauthorization. The voter ID legislation would impose new identification requirements for federal elections.

By conditioning Clayton's nomination on these legislative outcomes, Trump is using the vacant intelligence post as leverage to advance policy goals that have faced resistance in Congress. The tactic delays filling a position that oversees the nation's 18 intelligence agencies and coordinates national security information for the White House.

The strategy also extends Pulte's tenure as acting director despite the concerns that prompted Clayton's nomination in the first place. Trump told reporters the arrangement would continue until his replacement as U.S. attorney is confirmed, adding another condition to the timeline. The delay means the intelligence community will continue operating under acting leadership while Congress weighs the president's legislative demands.

cards.headline: Trump Threatens to Resume Bombing Iran Hours After G7 Backs Preliminary Deal
cards.body:
President Trump warned that the United States would resume military strikes against Iran if he became dissatisfied with a preliminary peace agreement between the two countries. The threat came just hours after leaders from the Group of 7 nations publicly endorsed the deal as a breakthrough.

The G7 leaders, gathered for their annual summit, issued a joint statement expressing support for the framework agreement and indicating their readiness to contribute to its implementation. The statement represented unified backing from major Western democracies and Japan for the diplomatic initiative aimed at ending the conflict between Washington and Tehran.

Trump made his threat during remarks to reporters following the G7 statement. He did not specify what conditions would trigger renewed bombing campaigns or which aspects of the preliminary agreement might prove unsatisfactory. He had previously indicated that potential targets for new attacks would include power stations and other civilian infrastructure.

The president's warning introduced fresh uncertainty into the diplomatic process. While international partners publicly championed the accord as a path toward regional stability, Trump's willingness to threaten military action underscored the conditional nature of his commitment to the agreement. His remarks raised questions about how other nations might respond should the United States withdraw from or abandon the framework.

Trump's stance contrasted sharply with his earlier statements that the United States was in a strong negotiating position and would "end up with a great deal." He announced an extension of a two-week ceasefire with Iran, citing requests from the Pakistani government and saying he would hold off on attacks until Iranian leaders submitted a unified peace proposal.

The preliminary agreement faces significant domestic skepticism. Many Senate Republicans expressed concerns about the deal's terms and said they needed thorough briefings before it was finalized. Senator Lindsey Graham, a close Trump ally and longtime Iran hawk, stated that descriptions of the agreement differed between how Iran and the United States characterized it, and said lawmakers needed to examine the actual terms carefully.

Iranian officials have expressed doubt about Trump's intentions. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the speaker of Iran's parliament who emerged as the regime's lead negotiator in recent talks, dismissed the ceasefire extension through an adviser, calling it "a ploy to buy time for a surprise strike."

The conflict between the United States and Iran had disrupted energy production and transportation throughout the Middle East, affecting global fuel costs. The preliminary agreement's full details have not been publicly disclosed, though CNN obtained a draft version of the memorandum of understanding. As Trump concludes his G7 summit meetings, observers expect he will face additional questions about the uncertain agreement and his broader foreign policy agenda.

cards.headline: Eight crew members killed in B-52 bomber crash at California air base
cards.body:
All eight people aboard a Boeing B-52 Stratofortress died when the aircraft crashed during a test flight at Edwards Air Force Base in California on Monday. The bomber plunged in a fiery explosion that sent thick plumes of smoke into the sky at the base located in the Mojave Desert, approximately 100 miles northeast of Los Angeles.

The investigation into the crash could take up to six months to complete, according to US Air Force officials. Investigators will examine flight data, maintenance records, and other factors that may have contributed to the accident. Early flight data indicates the aircraft descended at nearly a mile per minute before impact.

The Air Force has identified two of the victims. Lt. Col. Miles Middleton and Jeromy Smith, an engineer at the base, were among those who died. Smith's wife described him as a leader and a hero, mourning the loss of her husband in the tragedy.

The B-52 was conducting a test flight when the incident occurred at Edwards Air Force Base, which serves as a testing facility for military aircraft. The crash represents one of the deadliest incidents involving military aircraft at the base in recent years.

The deadly accident has renewed focus on the age of the B-52 bomber fleet. These strategic bombers have been in service for decades and continue to form a cornerstone of American air power since the Cold War era. The Air Force maintains these aircraft through regular upgrades and maintenance to keep them operational.

Edwards Air Force Base, located in southern California, has a long history as a center for aerospace testing and development. The sprawling facility in the Mojave Desert remains critical to military aviation research and evaluation.

The crash has devastated families of the victims, who are now mourning the loss of their loved ones. The Air Force has not yet released the identities of the six other crew members who died in the accident.

The base's emergency response teams worked swiftly following the incident. As the investigation proceeds, officials will work to determine what led to the test flight's tragic conclusion.

The B-52 Stratofortress has been a vital component of United States military capabilities for generations. The crash highlights ongoing questions about the age of the bomber fleet and the challenges of maintaining aircraft that have served in military operations for so many decades. Despite their age, the Air Force continues to rely on these bombers as essential elements of national defense strategy.

cards.headline: San Andreas and San Jacinto fault lines reach highest stress levels in 1,000 years
cards.body:
Two of Southern California's most dangerous earthquake fault systems have reached their highest levels of tectonic stress in a thousand years, according to new research published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth. Scientists say the region is now in a "critically loaded state" with significantly elevated earthquake risk.

Researchers at the University of Hawaii at Mānoa used computer modeling to analyze stress accumulation across the San Andreas and San Jacinto fault systems. By inputting 1,000 years of earthquake history into their model, they determined that current stress levels match or exceed the highest values recorded over the past millennium.

"Our results show that stress levels on multiple fault segments are now at or above the highest values seen in the past millennium and that the region may be capable of a large through-going rupture involving both fault systems," said Liliane Burkhard, the study's lead author.

A critical aspect of the research focuses on Cajon Pass, the location where the two faults intersect. Scientists describe this area as an "earthquake gate" that could either block large ruptures from traveling between the faults or allow both systems to rupture together in a single massive event. The conditions determining whether this gate opens appear to depend on how closely the stress levels on both fault systems align at the moment of rupture.

"Right now, with stress at historically high levels across the region and more than 160 years elapsed since the last major rupture, the system is in a critically loaded state," Burkhard said. More than a century has passed since the last significant earthquake on the southern San Andreas Fault, allowing stress to accumulate to unprecedented levels.

The research indicates that if both fault systems rupture simultaneously, the impacts could affect large areas across Southern California. However, Burkhard emphasized that the study does not predict when such an earthquake might occur.

"What we can say is that the system is critically stressed, and that physics-based models like this one give us a clearer picture of the range of scenarios we should be prepared for," she said.

The findings reinforce long-standing scientific warnings that Southern California faces significant seismic risk. The last major destructive earthquake to strike California was the 1994 Northridge earthquake in Los Angeles, which destroyed 87,000 homes and businesses and killed more than 60 people.

The research underscores why earthquake preparedness remains crucial for Southern California's millions of residents. Understanding the stress conditions on these fault systems helps scientists and emergency planners better prepare for potential seismic events and their consequences.

cards.headline: Israel Launches New Strikes on Lebanon Despite Trump Criticism
cards.teaser: Israel conducted fresh airstrikes on Lebanon after President Trump said Prime Minister Netanyahu needed to be more responsible regarding Lebanon.
cards.body:
Israel carried out fresh military strikes on Lebanese territory on Tuesday. President Trump publicly criticized the operations, telling reporters that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu needed to exercise greater responsibility regarding Lebanon.

The strikes proceeded despite Trump's remarks, demonstrating Israel's determination to continue its military campaign along its northern border. Trump's public criticism of Netanyahu's decisions marked an unusual moment of discord between the two leaders.

cards.headline: FBI Says Group Planned Attack on White House UFC Event Using Snipers and Drones
cards.teaser: A group allegedly planned to attack a UFC event at the White House using snipers and drones, according to newly unsealed court documents.
cards.body:
According to newly unsealed court filings, the FBI says a group plotted to attack a UFC event at the White House using snipers and drones. The alleged group expressed grievances about corruption, the Epstein files, and data centers.

The federal court documents that revealed the plot were previously sealed.

cards.headline: Trump Tells G7 Leaders 'I Am the Boss' as Summit Focuses on Ukraine
cards.teaser: President Trump told G7 leaders he is in charge during discussions that brought Ukraine back onto the summit agenda.
cards.body:
President Trump asserted his authority at the G7 summit while pledging support for Ukraine. He repeated his push for a settlement between Ukraine and Russia, calling the death toll "ridiculous" and urging Moscow to "make a deal." Trump claimed he had spoken with both Zelensky and Putin before the summit and said both leaders were open to meeting.

NATO Secretary General Rutte addressed changes to the U.S. commitment to the NATO Force Model, emphasizing that the adjustment reflects allies' need to fairly share security responsibilities rather than representing a U.S. withdrawal. He confirmed the U.S. remains committed to NATO while expecting greater burden-sharing from European partners.

cards.headline: Russian Warship Fires Warning Shots Near British Sailboat in English Channel
cards.teaser: A Russian naval frigate fired warning shots near a British couple's yacht in the English Channel, prompting condemnation from UK officials.
cards.body:
A Russian frigate fired warning shots near a British couple's sailboat in the English Channel. The retired couple told BBC Newsnight they attempted to signal the warship that they had changed course before the shots were fired.

Britain's Ministry of Defense stated the Russian vessel appeared to be attempting to avoid a collision during the encounter. Prime Minister Keir Starmer characterized the warship's actions as reckless, while the incident has intensified tensions between Russia and Western nations amid the ongoing Ukraine conflict.

cards.headline: Israel Launches New Strikes on Lebanon Despite Trump Criticism
cards.teaser: Israel conducted fresh airstrikes on Lebanon after President Trump said Prime Minister Netanyahu needed to be more responsible regarding Lebanon.
cards.body:
Israel carried out fresh military strikes on Lebanese territory on Tuesday. President Trump publicly criticized the operations, telling reporters that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu needed to exercise greater responsibility regarding Lebanon.

The strikes proceeded despite Trump's remarks, demonstrating Israel's determination to continue its military campaign along its northern border. Trump's public criticism of Netanyahu's decisions marked an unusual moment of discord between the two leaders.

cards.headline: South Africa's DA Leader Seeks to Remove Predecessor From Cabinet Post
cards.teaser: John Steenhuisen, leader of South Africa's second largest party, is calling for his predecessor to be dismissed as a minister.
cards.body:
John Steenhuisen, leader of South Africa's Democratic Alliance, is calling for his predecessor's removal from a ministerial post. Steenhuisen has led the DA, the country's second-largest political party, for seven years and is a prominent figure in South African politics.

The move reflects political tensions within South Africa's coalition government as party leaders jockey for influence and control over key positions.

cards.headline: Norway's Crown Princess Undergoes Successful Lung Transplant
cards.teaser: Crown Princess Mette-Marit received a lung transplant to treat pulmonary fibrosis and will spend several weeks recovering in hospital.
cards.body:
Crown Princess Mette-Marit of Norway has undergone a successful lung transplant, the royal palace announced. The procedure was completed without complications.

The crown princess had been suffering from pulmonary fibrosis, a chronic lung disease. She will spend several weeks recovering in hospital following the major surgery.

cards.headline: Equatorial Guinea Government Resigns After Failing to Meet Performance Targets
cards.teaser: The government of Equatorial Guinea resigned after the vice president said it had reached barely 10% of its targets.
cards.body:
Equatorial Guinea's government has resigned after failing to meet performance targets, according to an announcement by the country's vice president. The government achieved barely 10% of its objectives.

President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo has led the Central African nation since 1979. The mass cabinet resignation represents a significant political development, though details about the next government formation have not yet been announced.

cards.headline: South Africa Protesters Set Deadline for Undocumented Migrants to Leave
cards.teaser: Protesters in South Africa have given undocumented migrants until June 30 to leave the country, with reports of violence.
cards.body:
Protesters in South Africa have set June 30 as a deadline for undocumented migrants to leave the country. During confrontations, some migrants reported that protesters arrived carrying machetes.

The ultimatum reflects rising tensions over migration and economic competition in South Africa, which is home to millions of migrants from across the African continent. Many lack legal documentation. The campaign has sparked concerns about xenophobic violence, given South Africa's history of periodic attacks against foreign nationals.

cards.headline: Tropical storm may form near Texas coast as Louisiana issues warnings
cards.teaser: A weather system approaching the Gulf Coast could strengthen into Tropical Storm Arthur, prompting tropical storm warnings in Louisiana.
cards.body:
A tropical weather system approaching the Texas and Louisiana coasts may strengthen into Tropical Storm Arthur, which would be the first named storm of the Atlantic season. Tropical storm warnings have been issued in Louisiana as forecasters predict a major flood threat from heavy rainfall.

The system, currently designated as Potential Tropical Cyclone One, has already brought heavy rains to the Texas coast. Flooding is expected across Louisiana through Friday morning, and officials have opened sandbag distribution sites in South Mississippi. New Orleans leaders have outlined storm preparations as the region braces for severe weather and significant rainfall accumulation.

cards.headline: Federal prisons deny most inmate grievances over care and treatment
cards.teaser: An analysis of federal data shows the vast majority of prisoner grievances about abuse and denied medical care are rejected.
cards.body:
People in federal prison can file grievances about their treatment, including complaints about abuse and medical neglect. However, according to an analysis of federal data by The Marshall Project and NPR, these complaints rarely succeed.

The investigation found that federal prisons routinely reject inmate grievances and deny care for extended periods. Most complaints fail to produce results, leaving incarcerated people with limited options to address problems within the system.

cards.headline: Trump calls for delay in confirmation of intelligence chief nominee
cards.teaser: President Trump is asking the Senate to postpone the confirmation process for Jay Clayton, his nominee for Director of National Intelligence.
cards.body:
President Trump has halted the Senate confirmation process for Jay Clayton as Director of National Intelligence. The delay will allow Bill Pulte, Trump's controversial pick for acting director of national security, to remain in the role for several weeks longer.

Trump had initially pushed for Clayton's swift confirmation after Pulte's appointment as acting director faced bipartisan criticism and complicated efforts to renew the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act.

cards.headline: Israel strikes Lebanon despite Trump criticism of Netanyahu
cards.teaser: Israel launched new airstrikes on Lebanon after President Trump said Prime Minister Netanyahu needed to be more responsible.
cards.body:
Israel carried out new strikes on Lebanon on Tuesday, continuing its military operations in the region. During the G7 summit that day, President Trump publicly criticized Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, saying he needed to be more responsible regarding Lebanon.

Despite Trump's remarks, Israel proceeded with the strikes. The criticism represented an unusual public rebuke of Netanyahu from the American president, though it did not deter the Israeli government from its military actions.

cards.headline: Trump to hold press conference as G7 summit concludes
cards.teaser: President Trump is expected to answer questions at a press conference as the G7 summit wraps up.
cards.body:
President Trump is holding a press conference as the G7 summit concludes. The president has highlighted a tentative agreement with Iran that was discussed during the gathering of world leaders, and reporters are expected to question him about the deal and other summit outcomes.

The press conference comes at the end of several days of meetings with other G7 leaders. Key topics expected to be addressed include the uncertain agreement regarding Iran and U.S. support for Ukraine.

cards.headline: Norway's crown princess receives lung transplant
cards.teaser: Crown Princess Mette-Marit of Norway underwent a successful lung transplant and will spend several weeks recovering in hospital.
cards.body:
Crown Princess Mette-Marit of Norway has undergone a successful lung transplant, according to an announcement from the royal palace. The procedure addresses her pulmonary fibrosis, a condition characterized by lung tissue scarring that progressively impairs breathing.

The crown princess will spend several weeks recovering in hospital following the surgery. Pulmonary fibrosis often requires transplantation in advanced cases when the disease severely compromises lung function.

hero.headline: Oil Market Faces Potential Glut After Middle East Peace Deal
hero.body:
A peace agreement between the United States and Iran has triggered a dramatic reversal in oil market dynamics, with the International Energy Agency warning that global supply could soon outpace demand growth. The shift marks a sharp contrast to conditions during the conflict, when supply disruptions seemed imminent.

The recent memorandum of understanding, set for ceremonial signing in Geneva, centers on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and lifting the US naval blockade in the region. The agreement also includes financial incentives for Iran if it meets certain benchmarks. Both President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance have digitally signed the document, along with Iran's parliamentary speaker Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf on Tehran's behalf.

During the war, Middle East instability and concerns about disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz had created expectations of tight oil markets and higher prices. The IEA now projects that production capacity could outpace consumption as normalcy returns to the region, representing a significant challenge for energy producers who had ramped up output anticipating sustained high prices.

The timing of the peace deal arrives as California's jet fuel supply has dropped to levels unseen since 2023. As of April 17, the state held just over 2.6 million barrels of jet fuel, compared to 3.2 million barrels two years earlier, according to the California Energy Commission. California received 61.1 percent of its oil supply from foreign sources in 2025, a majority from Asian refiners. The supply disruption caused jet fuel prices to surge, with costs averaging $2.30 per gallon in early 2026 but reaching $4.19 per gallon by April 24. At Los Angeles International Airport, jet fuel costs climbed close to $15 per gallon.

According to Sandy Louey, a spokesperson for the California Energy Commission, "Jet fuel supply is tight globally. California prices reflect that pressure, though the US is better positioned due to domestic refining infrastructure and crude supply that Europe lacks."

The supply squeeze has prompted airlines including Delta, Southwest, and JetBlue to introduce increased baggage fees and fuel surcharges. Some travel experts predict that barring further geopolitical changes, shorter-haul flights that are less profitable will likely be cut, potentially snarling travel plans despite sustained passenger demand.

The shift from supply shock to potential oversupply illustrates how quickly energy markets can transform based on geopolitical developments. The IEA projection carries significant implications for energy policy and investment decisions. Producers may need to adjust output plans, while consuming nations could benefit from lower prices if the surplus materializes. However, the forecast depends on the durability of the peace agreement and whether production in Iran and neighboring countries returns to pre-conflict levels.

cards.headline: Federal Reserve Holds Interest Rates Steady at First Warsh Meeting
cards.teaser: The central bank is widely expected to keep rates unchanged as new chairman Kevin Warsh presides over his first policy decision.
cards.body:
The Federal Reserve is expected to hold interest rates steady at its meeting, marking the first policy decision under Chairman Kevin Warsh. The central bank's approach comes as officials assess economic conditions and inflation trends under new leadership.

Warsh takes over the Fed facing pressure from multiple directions, including tension within the institution and external political considerations. The recent peace agreement between the United States and Iran has simplified some inflation concerns that Warsh had been preparing to address when he assumed the role.

cards.headline: UK Inflation Holds Steady as Food Price Increases Slow
cards.teaser: Higher petrol prices were balanced by slower price rises for meat, dairy, and vegetables, according to official statistics.
cards.body:
UK inflation remained at 2.8% as moderating food prices counterbalanced rising petrol costs, according to the Office for National Statistics. Meat, dairy, and vegetable prices grew at their slowest pace in nearly 18 months, providing relief to household budgets after months of steeper increases.

The steadier inflation figures come amid broader economic scrutiny as the government navigates fiscal pressures and policy decisions ahead. The balance between energy costs and food price moderation reflects mixed signals in the UK's cost-of-living environment.

cards.headline: Japan Raids Ice Cream Manufacturers Over Price Fixing Allegations
cards.teaser: Regulators suspect six leading ice cream makers colluded to fix prices of popular frozen treats.
cards.body:
The Japan Fair Trade Commission raided six leading ice cream manufacturers as part of an investigation into suspected price fixing. Authorities believe the companies coordinated to set prices for popular frozen desserts sold across the country.

The timing of the investigation coincides with record summer temperatures across Japan. Japanese antitrust authorities have stepped up enforcement actions against cartels in recent years, particularly in consumer goods sectors where pricing coordination directly affects household expenses.

cards.headline: Prediction Markets Seek Wall Street Adoption for Institutional Trading
cards.teaser: Platforms that let millions bet on sports and pop culture now hope institutions will use them for hedging and big-ticket trades.
cards.body:
Prediction market platforms like Kalshi are pursuing Wall Street traders as their next major customer base after building businesses around wagering on sports and entertainment. The companies want financial institutions to adopt their platforms for hedging and other large-scale trading activities.

The push represents an expansion beyond the consumer-focused betting that has driven growth for prediction markets. Institutional adoption would require convincing professional traders that these platforms offer reliable pricing and sufficient liquidity for sophisticated financial strategies.

cards.headline: Small Businesses Struggle Under Tariff and Energy Cost Pressures
cards.teaser: Small business owners say relentless pressures from tariffs and higher energy prices have drained their finances and resilience.
cards.body:
Small businesses report that tariffs and higher energy prices have weakened their financial resilience. These combined pressures have depleted resources that could otherwise help them adapt to changing economic conditions.

The challenges facing smaller enterprises differ markedly from those of larger corporations, which have greater financial capacity to absorb cost increases. Small business owners say the current economic environment has limited their options for maintaining profitability while managing elevated input costs.

cards.headline: Spirit Airlines Airport Slots at LaGuardia Up for Sale in Bankruptcy
cards.teaser: A bankruptcy court has started selling the carrier's rights to fly from the New York City airport, but buyers may be scarce.
cards.body:
A bankruptcy court has begun the process of selling Spirit Airlines' rights to operate flights at LaGuardia Airport in New York. The slots are considered valuable assets, though finding a purchaser could prove difficult given current market conditions.

The sale is part of Spirit's bankruptcy proceedings as the budget carrier works to restructure its operations. LaGuardia slots are particularly prized because of the airport's proximity to Manhattan and capacity constraints that limit the number of flights allowed.

cards.headline: Uber to launch robotaxi service in Houston in 2027
cards.teaser: The ride-hailing company will expand its autonomous vehicle service to Houston as its second market.
cards.body: Uber will bring its premium robotaxi service to Houston in 2027, becoming the second city where the company operates autonomous rides. The vehicles will be Lucid electric cars equipped with self-driving technology from Nuro, and passengers will be able to request rides through the Uber app.

cards.headline: Pinterest launches AI-powered shopping app called Ask Pinterest
cards.teaser: The image-sharing platform has released an experimental app that uses conversational AI for product recommendations.
cards.body:
Pinterest has launched Ask Pinterest, an experimental AI-powered shopping app that uses conversational AI to help users find products and inspiration. Rather than scrolling through traditional feeds, users can ask questions in natural language and receive personalized recommendations based on their queries.

The app represents Pinterest's push to integrate artificial intelligence into its platform, shifting toward a more interactive shopping experience where users can seek advice and discover ideas through dialogue with the AI.

cards.headline: Cockroaches carry thousands of bacterial gene fragments in their genomes
cards.teaser: A study found that cockroaches harbor bacterial DNA, showing gene transfer happens beyond microbes.
cards.body:
Cockroaches carry thousands of pieces of bacterial genomes integrated into their own genetic material, according to new research. The finding demonstrates that horizontal gene transfer, where genetic material moves between different species, occurs in insects and not just in microorganisms.

Scientists found bacterial DNA fragments scattered throughout cockroach genomes, suggesting these genes were acquired from bacteria the insects encountered in their environment over evolutionary time. This discovery challenges previous assumptions about how genetic information spreads in nature.

cards.headline: NAACP lawsuit challenges xAI's use of gas turbines without air permits
cards.teaser: A civil rights organization alleges xAI operates turbines at a data center without required Clean Air Act permits.
cards.body:
The NAACP filed a lawsuit alleging that xAI uses gas turbines to power its Grok data center without obtaining required permits under the Clean Air Act. The Trump administration has moved to block the lawsuit from proceeding.

The case centers on whether xAI is operating power generation equipment in violation of federal air quality regulations. The NAACP claims the turbines, which provide electricity to the artificial intelligence data center, require environmental permits that the company has not secured.

cards.headline: Apple to move Hide My Email feature to different domain
cards.teaser: The privacy tool that generates anonymous email addresses will operate on a new domain in coming weeks.
cards.body:
Apple plans to change how its Hide My Email privacy feature works by moving anonymously generated email addresses to a different domain. The company will implement the change in the coming weeks.

Hide My Email allows users to create random email addresses that forward messages to their actual inbox, protecting their real email from being shared with apps and websites. The domain change could make the feature less effective, though Apple has not detailed how the modification will impact functionality.

cards.headline: Arianespace launches record-breaking payload for Amazon satellite network
cards.teaser: The European rocket company successfully deployed Amazon's internet satellites using its Ariane 6 rocket.
cards.body:
Arianespace launched its heaviest payload to date, deploying 36 satellites for Amazon's internet constellation. The mission used the upgraded Ariane 6 rocket with a more powerful booster configuration, marking a successful delivery for the European launch provider.

The launch represents progress for Amazon's satellite internet project, which has relied on European rockets while waiting for other launch providers. Swedish technology from Beyond Gravity was used to deploy the satellites once in orbit.

hero.headline: Real Madrid sign Bernardo Silva on free transfer from Manchester City
hero.body:
Real Madrid completed the signing of Bernardo Silva on a free transfer after the Portuguese midfielder left Manchester City at the end of the season. Silva joins the Spanish giants under new manager Jose Mourinho, reuniting with the coach who previously worked with Portuguese talent during his time at Porto and the national team setup.

The 32-year-old midfielder departed City after a decorated spell that saw him win multiple Premier League titles and contribute to the club's domestic and European success. His contract with City expired at the season's end, allowing him to negotiate a move without a transfer fee. Silva's technical ability and experience make him a significant addition to Mourinho's project at the Bernabeu.

Mourinho recently took charge at Real Madrid, bringing his tactical approach and winning mentality to one of European football's most storied clubs. The Portuguese manager has historically favored players he trusts and understands, making Silva's arrival a natural fit for his system. The midfielder's versatility allows him to operate in multiple positions across the middle of the park, giving Mourinho tactical flexibility.

Silva's move represents a shift in Real Madrid's transfer strategy, capitalizing on the opportunity to acquire an established player without the financial outlay of a transfer fee. The club can instead focus resources on Silva's wages and other squad reinforcements. His arrival adds depth and quality to a Madrid midfield that has undergone significant changes in recent seasons.

The signing positions Real Madrid to compete across multiple competitions next season. Silva brings Champions League pedigree and the ability to perform in high-pressure matches, qualities Mourinho values as he builds a squad capable of challenging for domestic and European honors. The partnership between manager and player will be closely watched as Madrid seeks to return to the top of Spanish and European football.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi delivers standout World Cup performance
cards.teaser: Messi topped a day of star performances at the World Cup, outshining Kylian Mbappe and Erling Haaland.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi made an immediate impact at the World Cup, scoring three goals in Argentina's opening match. The performance highlighted the exceptional goal-scoring talent on display at the tournament, which is less than a week old. France's Kylian Mbappé also impressed early, netting two goals in his team's opening game.

The early stages of the competition have showcased sublime finishing from the world's top strikers, with multiple superstars delivering strong performances in their opening matches.

cards.headline: Austria defeat World Cup debutants Jordan 3-1
cards.teaser: Marko Arnautovic scored a late penalty as Austria secured victory over Jordan in Group J.
cards.body:
Austria celebrated their return to the World Cup after 28 years with a 3-1 victory over Jordan in San Francisco. Romano Schmid gave Austria an early lead with a powerful strike in the 21st minute, but Jordan mounted a spirited comeback in the second half, with Ali Olwan equalizing with a precise effort that hit the post.

Substitute Marko Arnautovic sealed the win for Austria with a late penalty, delivering a strong start to their Group J campaign. Despite the defeat, Jordan showed determination in their World Cup debut, competing throughout in what proved to be an end-to-end encounter.

cards.headline: Matt Fisher takes wicket on England Test return after four years
cards.teaser: Fisher dismissed Devon Conway for nine runs in just his third over at The Oval.
cards.body:
Matt Fisher made an impressive return to Test cricket after a four-year absence, striking early on the opening day of England's second Test against New Zealand at The Oval. The fast bowler claimed the wicket of Devon Conway for nine runs in his third over.

Fisher's immediate impact provided England with a breakthrough as they began their match against the touring side.

cards.headline: Wout van Aert to miss Tour de France with elbow injury
cards.teaser: The Belgian cyclist will sit out next month's Tour de France due to an elbow injury.
cards.body:
Wout van Aert will miss next month's Tour de France after sustaining an elbow injury. The Belgian rider, one of cycling's most versatile competitors, has been ruled out of the sport's most prestigious race.

Van Aert's absence removes a key contender from the Tour de France field. The injury represents a significant setback for both the rider and his team as they prepare for the July race.

cards.headline: Danny Rohl leaves Rangers for Red Bull Salzburg
cards.teaser: The manager departs Rangers after eight months to take charge at the Austrian club.
cards.body:
Danny Röhl has left Rangers to become head coach of RB Salzburg by mutual agreement. The Austrian club will pay a seven-figure compensation package to Rangers for the manager, who spent eight months in charge at Ibrox after replacing Russell Martin in October. Röhl's backroom team, including performance manager Sascha Lense and first-team analyst Tristan Steiner, will also depart.

The managerial vacancy at Rangers comes as Derek McInnes emerges as a leading candidate for the position. McInnes is currently with Hearts and is being linked with a move to Ibrox.

cards.headline: France midfielder raises concerns over MetLife Stadium pitch quality
cards.teaser: Adrien Rabiot compared the pitch at the New York New Jersey Stadium to an artificial surface.
cards.body:
France midfielder Adrien Rabiot has voiced concerns about the playing surface at MetLife Stadium in New York, saying it resembles an artificial pitch. The comment comes as the venue prepares to host World Cup matches.

Rabiot's criticism highlights the challenges some teams face with pitch conditions at World Cup venues. His remarks suggest the grass surface at the New Jersey stadium may not meet the standards expected for international competition.

hero.headline: Mike Myers Confirms Fourth Austin Powers Film in Development
hero.body:
Mike Myers has confirmed that a fourth Austin Powers movie is in the works, though he provided minimal details about the project. The actor made the announcement during an appearance on Trevor Noah's World Cup Watch Party, responding to a fan question with a single-word affirmation.

Myers, who created and starred in the Austin Powers franchise, currently appears as the character in a new commercial for Verizon. The spy comedy series has been dormant since 2002's Austin Powers in Goldmember, which concluded a trilogy that began with 1997's Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery.

The original Austin Powers films became cultural phenomena in the late 1990s and early 2000s, with Myers playing multiple roles including the titular British spy and his nemesis Dr. Evil. The franchise grossed over $670 million worldwide and spawned countless catchphrases that entered popular culture.

Myers offered no elaboration on the new film's timeline, plot, or production status beyond his brief confirmation. The lack of detail leaves questions about when production might begin, which cast members might return, or what studio would distribute the project.

The announcement comes at a time when Hollywood has increasingly turned to reviving popular franchises from the 1990s and 2000s. The Austin Powers series has maintained a devoted fan base despite its two-decade absence from theaters, making it a potentially lucrative property for revival.

cards.headline: Prime Video Unveils 13 New Spanish Originals Led by Ester Expósito and Mario Casas
cards.teaser: The streaming service announced a slate of new productions in Madrid, including a second Zeta film and details of upcoming series.
cards.body:
Prime Video Spain announced 13 new titles and production updates at a Madrid event, reinforcing the platform's commitment to Spanish-language originals. The slate includes a second Zeta film featuring Mario Casas, who previously starred in Cross the Line, and the series Enfrentados: Marfil with Ester Expósito.

The announcement also highlighted Su Majestad Season 2, starring Anna Castillo from Nowhere. These reveals demonstrate Prime Video's continued investment in developing local content for the Spanish market.

cards.headline: Ginevra Elkann to Direct Film About Italy's Last Queen
cards.teaser: The historical drama will tell the story of Maria José of Savoy, who served as queen for only 27 days before Italy abolished its monarchy.
cards.body:
A new historical drama will chronicle the life of Maria José of Savoy, who became queen of Italy after World War II but held the position for just 27 days before Italians voted to end the monarchy. The film will be directed by Ginevra Elkann alongside Marco Bellocchio.

Maria José's brief reign marked the end of the House of Savoy's rule over Italy, which had lasted since the country's unification in the 19th century.

cards.headline: Indonesian Director Ismail Basbeth Sets Next Feature Film
cards.teaser: The filmmaker announced Love Letters of Our Life while presenting his latest work at the Shanghai International Film Festival.
cards.body:
Indonesian director Ismail Basbeth has announced Love Letters of Our Life as his next feature project.

Basbeth made the announcement while attending the Shanghai International Film Festival, where his current film My Own Last Supper had its world premiere as part of the main competition. The festival appearance marks another step in the director's growing international profile.

cards.headline: TV Presenter Ashley Cain Accused of Using Sexist Language
cards.teaser: The former footballer, known for hosting BBC Three's Ashley Cain: Into the Danger Zone, faces allegations of misogynistic behavior.
cards.body:
Television personality Ashley Cain has been accused of using sexist and misogynistic language. The former footballer currently presents Ashley Cain: Into the Danger Zone on BBC Three.

Cain transitioned from professional football to television presenting, building a public profile through his hosting work. The allegations represent a challenge to his media career at a time when the entertainment industry faces increased scrutiny over workplace conduct.

cards.headline: Streaming Executives See Asian Content as Key Growth Driver
cards.teaser: Netflix, Prime Video, Disney and Warner Bros. Discovery representatives gathered at APOS 2026 in Bali to discuss the region's growing importance.
cards.body:
Streaming giants Netflix, Prime Video, Disney, and Warner Bros. Discovery gathered at the APOS 2026 conference in Bali to discuss the strategic importance of Asian content. The executives emphasized that Asian intellectual property and local storytelling have evolved from regional offerings into valuable global assets for their platforms.

During a session titled "Asia's Streaming Advantage: Growth, Profitability and What's Next," Netflix's vice president of content participated in conversations about how streaming services are reshaping their international strategies. The conference underscored a significant industry shift, with platforms increasingly positioning Asian productions as central rather than supplementary to their worldwide operations.

cards.headline: Australian Director Warwick Thornton Presents Wolfram at Shanghai Festival
cards.teaser: The filmmaker discussed his latest feature, which competed at the Berlin Film Festival earlier this year, following its Chinese premiere.
cards.body:
Australian director Warwick Thornton attended a post-screening event at the Shanghai International Film Festival following the Chinese premiere of his latest feature, Wolfram. The film was previously selected for the main competition at the Berlin Film Festival earlier in 2026.

Thornton discussed the film's roots in family history at the Shanghai event, continuing his exploration of Australian experiences through cinema.

hero.headline: Trump delays intelligence chief nomination, ties confirmation to voting legislation
hero.body:
President Trump announced Wednesday that he is pausing the confirmation process for Jay Clayton, his nominee for Director of National Intelligence, until Congress passes legislation on warrantless surveillance powers and voter identification requirements. The Senate had been scheduled to begin confirmation hearings for Clayton, a federal prosecutor, on Wednesday.

Trump said Clayton's hearing would be delayed until Congress approves both the extension of warrantless spy powers and a voter identification bill. The president indicated that acting Director of National Intelligence Bill Pulte will remain in the position during the delay. Trump had originally nominated Clayton to address concerns from lawmakers that Pulte lacked sufficient experience for the intelligence role.

The move links a key national security appointment to unrelated legislative priorities. The warrantless surveillance powers in question allow intelligence agencies to collect communications of foreign targets without obtaining individual warrants, a program that requires periodic congressional reauthorization. The voter ID legislation would impose new identification requirements for federal elections.

By conditioning Clayton's nomination on these legislative outcomes, Trump is using the vacant intelligence post as leverage to advance policy goals that have faced resistance in Congress. The tactic delays filling a position that oversees the nation's 18 intelligence agencies and coordinates national security information for the White House.

The strategy also extends Pulte's tenure as acting director despite the concerns that prompted Clayton's nomination in the first place. Trump told reporters the arrangement would continue until his replacement as U.S. attorney is confirmed, adding another condition to the timeline. The delay means the intelligence community will continue operating under acting leadership while Congress weighs the president's legislative demands.

cards.headline: Trump says Iran agreement not final, threatens renewed military action
cards.teaser: President Trump said the memorandum of understanding with Tehran remains tentative and warned of resumed strikes if Iran fails to comply.
cards.body:
President Trump said Wednesday that the memorandum of understanding with Iran is not a final agreement and warned the U.S. could resume military strikes if Iran fails to comply with its terms. Trump told reporters the deal could be reversed if he determines it is not working.

The tentative ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran is set for 60 days. The agreement follows months of conflict that disrupted global energy markets and destabilized the region, including impacts on Lebanon and international food supplies.

cards.headline: Senate Democrats press credit bureaus over student loan reporting errors
cards.teaser: Elizabeth Warren and Democratic colleagues are demanding answers about incorrect credit reports linked to federal student loan servicers.
cards.body:
Senate Banking Committee ranking member Elizabeth Warren and other Democratic senators sent a letter to Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion on Wednesday, raising concerns about inaccurate credit reports stemming from federal student loan servicers.

The lawmakers are calling on the three largest U.S. credit bureaus to address what they describe as unchecked errors from student loan servicers. These reporting mistakes could harm borrowers' credit scores and overall financial standing.

cards.headline: Acting attorney general faces Republican resistance in Senate
cards.teaser: Todd Blanche encountered criticism from GOP senators who questioned his independence from President Trump during a private meeting.
cards.body:
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche is heading into a difficult Senate confirmation process as he seeks permanent appointment to the role. More than 20 Republican senators raised concerns about his credibility and independence from President Trump during a private meeting last month.

Several GOP lawmakers expressed doubts about whether Blanche can maintain sufficient distance from the president in making prosecutorial decisions. The skepticism from members of his own party suggests a challenging path to confirmation.

cards.headline: Justice Department investigation gives Newsom political opening
cards.teaser: California Governor Gavin Newsom is using a DOJ probe as an opportunity to raise his national profile ahead of the 2028 presidential race.
cards.body:
California Governor Gavin Newsom is embracing a Department of Justice investigation rather than treating it as a political liability. The Democratic governor, viewed as a leading contender for the White House in 2028, is using the confrontation with President Trump to elevate his national standing.

Newsom is framing the DOJ investigation as a way to cement his role as a prominent Trump opponent within the Democratic Party. The approach suggests he sees the federal scrutiny as a chance to demonstrate resistance to the administration rather than a threat to his political future.

cards.headline: Republicans target Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner in midterm strategy
cards.teaser: GOP strategists are focusing on the progressive Democrat challenging Susan Collins as they work to maintain Senate control.
cards.body:
Republicans are elevating Graham Platner, the progressive Democrat running against Senator Susan Collins in Maine, as a central figure in their midterm election messaging. Platner, a combat veteran and oyster farmer, won the Democratic primary last week after an insurgent campaign that reshaped Maine politics.

The GOP is using Platner as a foil in their effort to retain Senate seats this fall. Republican strategists view the Maine race as an opportunity to frame Democrats as too progressive for moderate voters in competitive states.

cards.headline: Democratic socialists advance infrastructure-focused policies in major cities
cards.teaser: Progressive candidates in New York, Seattle, and Washington are championing government programs for housing, child care, and transit.
cards.body:
Democratic socialists in several major American cities are promoting what they call sewer socialism, a policy approach focused on expanding government services for public benefit. Candidates including New York's Zohran Mamdani, Seattle's Katie Wilson, and Washington D.C. mayoral candidate Janeese Lewis George are centering their campaigns on these proposals.

The platform emphasizes government programs for affordable housing, child care, and public transportation. The movement takes its name from early 20th century Milwaukee politicians who prioritized municipal infrastructure and services.
